<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Planning a solution for styled boxes around definitions, theorems, and propositions.

A Jekyll plugin will register custom tags for definitions, theorems, and related environments. CSS will style the resulting boxes. The design follows the existing `details` pattern. Optional titles will be supported. Auto-numbering is deferred; custom labels will be used instead.

Separate tags like `{% definition %}` and `{% theorem %}` were chosen over a generic `mathbox` tag. Proof blocks will end with a QED symbol. Each environment gets a distinct color: blue for definitions, purple for theorems, and theme-aware palettes.

Color assignments are now set: teal for propositions, lighter blue for lemmas, orange for corollaries, gray for remarks, green for examples, and subtle neutral for proofs. CSS variables in `_themes.scss` will support dark mode. The CTMC post will serve as a live example. The plugin file is being created.

The plugin will inherit from `Liquid::Block` and use a base class modeled after `details.rb`. An `ENVIRONMENTS` hash maps each tag name to its display label. The constructor extracts the environment type and optional title from the tag markup.

The plugin converts markdown titles and body content through Jekyll's Markdown converter. Proof blocks append a QED symbol. Empty titles fall back to the environment label.

The plugin will wrap rendered content in a div with a class matching the environment type. The author is refining how titles appear inside headers, considering standard math typography conventions such as parenthetical labels or numbered labels.

Headers will read "Definition (Counting process)" when a title is given, or simply "Definition" otherwise. Proof headers always end with a period, becoming "Proof." or "Proof (sketch)."

The CSS will be scoped to `d-article` and centered in the text grid. Each environment variant receives a unique left border and header color. Body paragraphs will lose their top and bottom margins. Dark mode backgrounds will be muted for readability.

The counting process definition near line 153 of the CTMC post will be converted as a live example. The obsidian-to-distill skill will be skipped since it was not requested. Liquid block tags automatically generate their end variants, so manual registration is unnecessary. A Jekyll build will verify plugin loading and rendering.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — I added styled math environment boxes for Distill posts. They work like the existing `{% details %}` tag: write markdown inside, and each environment gets its own color and label.

### Usage

```markdown
{% definition Counting process %}
A counting process $C_t$ is one that:
1. takes values in the non-negative integers;
2. is non-decreasing: $C_t \geq C_{t^{\prime}}$ for $t \geq t^{\prime}$.
{% enddefinition %}

{% theorem %}
...
{% endtheorem %}

{% proof %}
...
{% endproof %}

{% proof of Theorem 1 %}
...
{% endproof %}
```

**Available tags:** `definition`, `theorem`, `proposition`, `lemma`, `corollary`, `remark`, `example`, `proof`

- Optional title after the tag name → `Definition (Counting process)`
- `proof` without a title → **Proof.** with a ∎ at the end
- `proof` with a title → **Proof (of Theorem 1).**

### What was added

1. **`_plugins/mathbox.rb`** — Jekyll Liquid tags (same pattern as `details.rb`)
2. **`_sass/_distill.scss`** — box styling scoped to `d-article`, with `grid-column: text`
3. **`_sass/_themes.scss`** — per-environment accent/background colors for light and dark themes

Each environment has a distinct left-border accent:

| Environment | Color |
|---|---|
| Definition | Blue |
| Theorem | Purple (theme) |
| Proposition | Teal |
| Lemma | Soft blue |
| Corollary | Amber |
| Remark | Gray |
| Example | Green |
| Proof | Neutral gray |

I also converted the **Counting process** and **Poisson process** definitions in your CTMC post as examples. Preview with `bundle exec jekyll serve` to see them in context.

If you want auto-numbering (Definition 1, Theorem 2, …) or cross-references, say the word and we can add that next.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

It's a **Kramdown escaping issue**, same family as the smart-quotes/prime problem in your obsidian-to-distill skill.

### What happens

You wrote LaTeX-style escaped braces:

```markdown
$o(t) = \{ f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}} \mid ... \}$
```

Kramdown strips the backslashes before KaTeX sees the math, so the HTML becomes:

```html
$o(t) = { f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}} \mid ... }$
```

In KaTeX, bare `{` and `}` are **grouping delimiters**, not visible characters. So the set braces disappear — you get something like $o(t) = f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}} \mid \ldots$ instead of $\{ f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}} \mid \ldots \}$.

### Fix

Double the backslashes so one survives Kramdown:

```markdown
$o(t) = \\{ f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}} \mid \lim_{t \to 0} f(t)/t = 0 \\}$
```

Alternative: use `\lbrace` / `\rbrace`, which Kramdown leaves alone.

I fixed all six affected spots in the CTMC post (lines 173, 194, 202, 213, 217, 220). Jekyll serve should auto-reload — refresh and the braces should show up.
